item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00108","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C04","C09"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 is a direct and material drafting source for the later proclamation. It develops the same policy and legal predicates later condensed into the child's recitals: Soviet obstruction of a peace treaty with a unified Germany, removal of Germany's enemy status and associated disabilities, preservation of occupation rights derived from conquest and Allied supreme authority, preservation of war-derived rights and privileges, and termination through legislation followed by presidential proclamation. C04 concerns Germany's occupation administration but lacks the child's termination framework. C09 offers a superficially parallel termination-proclamation form, but only as routine proclamation machinery in an unrelated trade-agreement context.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"efforts to this end have been frustrated and made impossible for the time being by the policy of the Soviet Government","parent_excerpt":"Soviet Russia has actively prevented the growth of a representative democratic government in a unified Germany, and has thus made impossible for the time being the arrangement of a final peace settlement","explanation":"Distinctive shared factual and policy predicate, closely condensed in the child."},{"child_excerpt":"bring the existing state of war with Germany to a close and to remove Germany from its present enemy status, thus eliminating certain disabilities affecting German nationals","parent_excerpt":"bringing the existing technical state of war to a close ... thus lifting Germany from its present enemy status ... General disabilities of this kind will be eliminated by the termination of the present state of war","explanation":"The child closely combines several characteristic formulations from C02."},{"child_excerpt":"The rights ... of the United States and the other occupation powers in Germany ... derive from the conquest of Germany and the assumption of supreme authority by the Allies and are not affected by the termination of the state of war","parent_excerpt":"The rights of the occupying powers ... will not be affected by its legal termination. The fights of the occupying powers result from the conquest of Germany ... and the Allied assumption of supreme authority.","explanation":"Near-literal transfer of a distinctive legal rationale."},{"child_excerpt":"the Congress of the United States by a joint resolution ... has resolved that the state of war ... is terminated ... Now, Therefore ... pursuant to such joint resolution, do proclaim","parent_excerpt":"the best method for terminating the state of war with Germany would be by the enactment of appropriate legislation in advance of the issuance of a Presidential proclamation","explanation":"The child implements the precise legislation-then-proclamation sequence recommended in C02."}]}
